method: Masks and CPU lists are parsed locally with exact big-integer arithmetic. A hex mask accepts hexadecimal digits with an optional 0x prefix, spaces or underscores; bit n is logical CPU n, and any bit at or above the configured CPU count is rejected with the offending index. A CPU list accepts comma- or space-separated indices and low-to-high ranges, silently deduplicates overlaps, sorts the result, and rejects descending ranges or indices beyond the CPU count. The CPU count must be a whole number from 1 to 1024, matching the kernel's CPU_SETSIZE limit; larger decimal outputs are exact because BigInt is used rather than 32-bit bitwise operators. Ranges are compressed for the CPU list, taskset -c, Docker --cpuset-cpus and cgroup v2 cpuset.cpus forms, the systemd CPUAffinity value uses a space-separated list of indices and ranges, and the taskset mask form prints the bare lowercase hexadecimal value. Binary output is grouped in nibbles from the high bit. The tool reports an empty selection instead of inventing a CPU, and it neither executes commands nor uses storage, uploads or network access.
